title: How to choose a cross-stitch hoop size
subtitle: Matching hoop diameter to project size and personal working style
excerpt: A cross-stitch hoop should be large enough to hold the design area comfortably without re-hooping too often, but not so large that the fabric cannot be kept taut. A good rule of thumb is to choose a hoop that gives at least 3–4 cm of clear Aida around the stitching area so the hoop ring sits on unstitched fabric.
sourceNotes: Hoop size selection for cross-stitch. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.

content.text: Hoop size is usually expressed as the inner diameter of the inner ring in centimetres. For cross-stitch, the most useful range is 10 cm to 25 cm. The right hoop lets you work a full session without re-hooping, while keeping the
taut across the whole stitching area.

Measure the stitching area of the design: the full height and width of the charted design in centimetres. For a design that stitches out at 12 × 10 cm, the minimum hoop size is the larger dimension plus 6–8 cm for the hoop border. This gives a minimum hoop of about 18–20 cm.
For a small design (under 8 cm in either direction), a 10 or 13 cm hoop is sufficient and is easier to hold and manoeuvre. A large hoop on a small design makes the project feel unwieldy.

For a large design, a hoop that covers the entire design area in one mounting is ideal. This avoids hoop marks in the stitched area. If re-hooping is unavoidable, wrap the inner hoop with twill tape to reduce mark depth.

Consider material as well as size. Wooden hoops grip Aida better than plastic at the same diameter. Bamboo hoops are lighter than wood for the same diameter. Plastic hoops are smooth and mark the fabric less, but may require wrapping to improve grip.

Check that the chosen hoop fits comfortably in the hand. A 25 cm hoop cannot be gripped one-handed easily; it usually requires a table stand or floor stand. A 15 cm hoop sits comfortably in the non-dominant hand for one-handed stitching. The right size should feel secure when held at the edge.

items.symptom: The hoop leaves a permanent ring mark on the Aida
items.cause: The hoop is left in place for too long, or the inner ring is too smooth and presses into the fabric.
items.fix: Remove the hoop at the end of each stitching session. Wrap the inner ring with cotton twill tape to cushion the grip. If a mark is already present, dampen and press the Aida from the back to remove it.

items.symptom: The fabric keeps slipping out of the hoop mid-session
items.cause: The hoop is too large for the fabric or the screw cannot be tightened enough to hold it.
items.fix: Choose a hoop one size smaller. Alternatively, wrap the inner ring with tape to add grip. Do not try to hold the fabric with extra tightening; over-tightening distorts the Aida squares.

content.text: A set of three hoops in different sizes — 10 cm, 15 cm, and 20 cm — covers most cross-stitch projects. The 10 cm hoop suits small motifs and sampler sections; the 15 cm hoop suits most beginner-to-intermediate projects; the 20 cm hoop handles larger designs. Having the right hoop to hand from the start makes the mounting step straightforward.
